senses.gloss:
Pṛdāku, the name of a ‘snake’ in the Atharvaveda, is mentioned in the list of victims at the aśvamedha (‘horse sacrifice’), in the yajurveda Saṃhitās, and occasionally else where. Its skin was specially valuable, according to the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes i. 27, 1; iii. 27, 3; vi. 38, 1; vii. 56, 1; x. 4, 11 et seq.; xii. 3, 57.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 5, 10, 1; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 14; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 33.
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, vi. 12; Sāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, xii. 27.
i. 27. 1.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 94.

Pṛdāku-sānu, ‘having the surface of a snake,’ is taken by Ludwig and Griffith as the name of the institutor of a sacrifice in one hymn of the Rigveda.
Foot notes Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 161.
Hymns of the Rigveda, 2, 141.
viii. 17, 15.
